items.summary: MHA constituted a committee to examine alternative protest venues; based on its recommendations, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar issued a notice de-notifying Jantar Mantar as a designated protest venue. Three new venues designated: Ramlila Ground (Central Delhi), Burari Ground (North Delhi), CBD Ground (East Delhi); a detailed revised SOP governing protests at the three venues to be issued separately. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacted on his own Instagram reel (~2:16 PM IST, ~140K likes): 'Today, Modi denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Tomorrow, he will denotify democracy itself. The dictator's problem was never the protest site. It was the very idea of people protesting.' Corroborated by 7Globe (India News), news89 (citing India Today) and currentaffairs.adda247. Never logged by any earlier run; caught up this run.
items.title: Delhi Police officially de-notified Jantar Mantar as a protest site; three new venues designated

items.summary: Delhi High Court will hear TWO protest-linked petitions on Tuesday Oct 13: (1) the plea on the alleged closure of Jantar Mantar as a protest site (already tracked); (2) a NEW petition alleging 'outsiders' entered the weekend protest and harassed the demonstrators. The bench of Acting CJ Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma declined an urgent Monday hearing, saying the Supreme Court is 'equally seized' of the matter and has called on the Union to file affidavits. Mentioning counsel: 'Now today Jantar Mantar is also closed. There is no other place which has been earmarked... Peaceful protests are being quelled today... We have faced this in 1975.' Single-sourced (News89); watch for corroboration.
items.title: Delhi HC to hear two protest petitions Tuesday: Jantar Mantar closure + 'outsiders harassed protesters' plea

items.summary: FIRST outcome reporting on the 1:30 PM IST Chalo Dilli march (now ~1.1h in): (a) verified Newslaundry field report by Sreenivasan Jain from outside Constitution House - opposition leaders gathered preparing to march to the Supreme Court; police and paramilitary lines deployed to block the march route; supporters initially kept inside the compound, then moved away; he interviewed Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury. (b) Verified @iycmadhyapradesh reel (~2:44 PM IST) shows thousands of people marching down Barakhamba Road, police observing from the side - the march IS in motion with large turnout. (c) news89 recap: demonstrators sat on roads, traffic ground to a halt around Mandi House Circle; HP CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu among those assembled near Himachal Bhavan/Mandi House. The Jagran live blog's newest entry remains 01:52 PM IST (pre-march) with no outcome text yet.
items.title: Chalo Dilli march in motion with thousands; blocked cordon at Constitution House

items.summary: Verified Dainik Bhaskar street interview (4.6M followers) at the Delhi march: a woman leader identifying herself as from Panipat representing the All India Mahila Congress alleged that RSS and BJP workers are attacking women protesters and that police used spray against them; she says the women now carry pepper spray for protection. A single-sourced participant claim via a verified news account; police have not responded. First spray-use allegation of the day.
items.title: Mahila Congress leader alleges police used spray against women protesters
Shivraj Singh Chouhan calls INDIA bloc march 'drama'
items.summary: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan called the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court a 'drama', saying Congress is trying to 'create anarchy by spreading falsehood in its bid to come to power'. (The Daily Jagran INDIA-bloc live blog, 02:57 PM IST entry)

items.title: CJI's letter: meeting declined on 'separation of powers' principle
items.summary: Details of CJI Surya Kant's letter declining the INDIA bloc meeting request: the meeting would be 'against the principle of separation of powers', per India Today reporting cited on the Jagran live blog (02:28 PM IST entry). The CJI's response was sent to the opposition leaders' official email on Sunday night.
items.source_name: India Today via The Daily Jagran

items.title: Abhijeet Dipke's new personal post: Modi 'a fascist dictator'
items.summary: New top post on @abhijeetdipke (~66K likes, ~780 comments within minutes): 'Waging war against your own countrymen. You’re showing the country exactly what you are: a fascist dictator, @narendramodi.' First direct public statement from the founder since reaching Hingoli for his grandmother's last rites — a personal-rhetoric escalation while Das and Ranka lead from Delhi. Provider returned no post timestamp; ranked newest at the ~3:10 PM IST fetch and absent from the 2:47 PM IST check.

First outcome reporting on the 'Chalo Dilli' march (which began ~1:30 PM IST from Connaught Place toward the Supreme Court): a large INDIA bloc demonstration made its way through central Delhi and reached the Constitution Club of India by ~2:05 PM IST. Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Mallikarjun Kharge and Mamata Banerjee arrived at the venue. KC Venugopal called it the 'biggest andolan' against the Election Commission and said the alliance will also file its Supreme Court petition. RJD's Tejashwi Yadav joined with sharp remarks ('Democracy is being crushed... Elections must be fair'), and Himachal CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said the Congress will submit memoranda to constitutional bodies. Heavy security (Delhi Police, RAF) continued around the route; march to the SC still in motion at report time.
items.title: Chalo Dilli march reaches Constitution Club; Rahul, Kharge, Mamata, Tejashwi join

items.summary: Two BJP chief ministers hit out at the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court on Monday. Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis told ANI the opposition was trying to 'undermine public trust in judicial institutions,' asking 'Where does the Constitution state that the Chief Justice of India has to meet a protest march?' and calling the opposition 'anti-constitutional.' Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma, in an X post, accused Rahul Gandhi and Congress of questioning electoral outcomes selectively ('When PM Modi is elected Prime Minister, Rahul Gandhi calls it manipulation, yet his own election to Parliament... is beyond question'). First CM-level ruling-party counter to Monday's march beyond the logged Chouhan 'drama' remark.
items.title: Fadnavis, Himanta Sarma slam INDIA bloc's SC march as anti-constitutional

items.summary: AAP called a meeting of its Delhi MLAs and councillors to plan week-long protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alongside the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Dilli' march from Connaught Place to the Supreme Court. The same report notes high security across central Delhi with metro station entry/exit restricted until 4 PM on Oct 12. First report of a multi-day protest plan from AAP.
items.title: AAP calls meeting to plan week-long protests against CEC
INDIA bloc's Chalo Dilli march leaves Constitution Club, heads for the Supreme Court
items.summary: First concrete reporting of the march-to-SC phase: a bus carrying Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra plus other INDIA bloc leaders left the Constitution Club ~3:11 PM IST for the Barakhamba Road junction to start the 'March for Democracy' to the Supreme Court (PTI video via the live blog); protesters gathered at Barakhamba Road ~3:20 PM IST; by ~3:23 PM IST Rahul Gandhi was leading the march to the SC, where leaders plan to file the vote-chori petition against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

items.title: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and AISA chief Neha Bora marching in 'Dilli Chalo' protest toward the SC
items.summary: The Jagran day-3 live blog's newest entry (04:37 PM IST, Oct 12) confirms Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and AISA president Neha Bora are participating in the 'Dilli Chalo' march, demanding action against and the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Neha Bora marching alongside the INDIA-bloc leadership is new — she was detained on Saturday evening (released Oct 10, phone returned). A companion 04:26 PM IST entry ('Akhilesh Yadav joins agitation') repeats the already-alerted 12:00 PM IST march confirmation; 04:15 PM IST ANI visuals (Statesman House) and a 03:58 PM IST Mandi House security note are march-in-motion color with no new facts. Petition-filing outcome still not reported.
items.source_name: The Daily Jagran (INDIA-bloc day-3 live blog)

items.title: Claim: AAP leaders detained on Oct 12 while marching toward Connaught Place
items.summary: A verified Firstpost Instagram roundup carousel (published 10:58:26Z, ~4:28 PM IST Oct 12) reports that AAP leaders were detained on Oct 12 while marching toward Connaught Place. No names, times or detention locations given, and no other outlet corroborated it in this run — single-sourced, watch for corroboration. The same carousel recaps already-logged facts: ~500 detained in Oct 11 flash protests (student activists, CPI(M) MP John Brittas, journalists), the Jantar Mantar de-notification (Ramlila/Burari/CBD replacement venues), and six metro stations restricted 6 AM-4 PM Oct 12.

items.title: DMRC reopens entry/exit gates at ALL Delhi Metro stations
items.summary: DMRC said entry and exit gates at all stations across the Delhi Metro network have been reopened, hours after security restrictions were imposed at six stations (Rajiv Chowk, Janpath, Mandi House, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Barakhamba Road) due to the INDIA-bloc protest march. First lifting of Monday's transport curbs.
items.source_name: DMRC via thedailyjagran.com (India bloc march live blog)

items.title: Police stop INDIA-bloc march at barricaded Bhagwan Das Road
items.summary: PTI reports police stopped the opposition 'Dilli Chalo' march at the barricaded Bhagwan Das Road as it moved toward the Supreme Court. First police halt on the march route; no detention reporting yet. Follows the earlier reported leaders' bus ride to Barakhamba Road (~3:11 PM IST).
items.source_name: PTI via thedailyjagran.com (India bloc march live blog)

items.title: Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav lead foot march to SC after bus stopped mid-way
items.summary: Visuals show Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and other opposition leaders leading the 'Dilli Chalo' march on foot, accompanied by hundreds of supporters, after their bus was stopped mid-way; AISA president Neha Bora also joined the agitation. Advances the march-to-SC phase (previously reported bus movement) into a foot-march phase; SC petition-filing outcome still unreported.

Rahul Gandhi filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court against the Election Commission of India challenging the SIR process (per LiveLaw, via the Jagran live blog). This is the petition-filing outcome the watch has been tracking all afternoon; the blog's headline says his legal team filed it after police stopped the foot march at Bhagwan Das Road. Earlier plans (CJI declined a meeting, asked them to file) now executed.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi files writ petition in SC against ECI over SIR

items.summary: Police added more barricades on Bhagwan Das Road amid the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Follows the earlier stoppage of the opposition march at the barricaded Bhagwan Das Road (~4:48 PM IST); security posture tightening even as metro curbs were lifted.
items.title: Police add more barricades on Bhagwan Das Road

items.summary: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and Telangana CM Revanth Reddy protested against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi. Tejashwi and Akhilesh were already on the march; Revanth Reddy joining is new.
items.title: Tejashwi, Akhilesh and Telangana CM Revanth Reddy protest against CEC
CJP submits formal letter to Delhi Police seeking a Jantar Mantar protest date; 24-hour ultimatum now in writing
items.summary: CJP submitted a formal representation to the DCP, Parliament Street Police Station, asking police to pick a date of their choosing for a peaceful Jantar Mantar demonstration (flipping the 10-day notice rule back on the police) and to de-escalate law-enforcement presence. The letter alleges 'severe disruption and widespread public distress' with over 55,000 police and paramilitary personnel deployed, citing arbitrary detentions, physical aggression and prolonged custody, plus financial strain on businesses from road closures. It warns that if police do not respond within 24 hours of receipt, CJP will continue protesting peacefully and announce a mass-protest date. Ashutosh Ranka added that the DCP, Additional DCP and SHO were all absent when the delegation arrived. Note: Saurav Das and Ranka handed the letter in during the already-alerted 10 AM IST PS visit; this is the first publication of the letter's full text and claims.

items.title: Police pushed back protesters near Barakhamba Road during INDIA bloc SC march
items.summary: Delhi Police pushed back protesters near Barakhamba Road during the INDIA bloc's 'March for Democracy' to the Supreme Court against CEC Gyanesh Kumar (thedailyjagran day-3 live blog, 05:47 PM IST entry — landed after the prior run's full-page check; distinct from the earlier-logged ~4:48 PM IST stoppage at Bhagwan Das Road). No detentions or injuries reported in the entry.

items.title: Traffic police: Mandi House roads affected, 'maximum available force' deployed
items.summary: Amid the INDIA bloc march, Additional Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Dinesh Kumar Gupta said Mandi House and roads in the division are affected: 'substantial force has been deployed. We have deployed our maximum available force; traffic is being properly regulated, and we are issuing advisories accordingly' (thedailyjagran day-3 live blog, 06:06 PM IST entry).

items.title: Dhruv Rathee claims he is 'unofficially under house arrest' with police surveillance
items.summary: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee (released ~3 AM IST Oct 11 after the Jantar Mantar crackdown) claims he is 'unofficially' under house arrest: ~50 police personnel stationed outside his residence, being followed wherever he goes, and threatened with immediate detention if he goes near a protest; he said he wanted to join Monday's INDIA bloc march to the SC but was prevented (reported by thedailyjagran via Lallantop; article published 12:58 PM IST Oct 12 — pre-baseline but never logged by earlier runs; self-reported, not independently corroborated).

Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra reached the Supreme Court after the INDIA bloc's legal team filed the writ petition against the ECI, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the two ECs over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls. This closes out the day's march arc: foot march from the barricaded Bhagwan Das Road to the court itself.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi reach Supreme Court after legal team files SIR writ petition against ECI

items.summary: Mallikarjun Kharge, who is one of the petitioners in the SIR writ plea, reached the Supreme Court along with several other Congress and opposition leaders; visuals show Kharge inside the court with Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar, former Chhattisgarh CM Bhupesh Baghel and others. Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Akhilesh Yadav were also reported at the SC. The petition names the ECI, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners as respondents.
items.title: Kharge, a named petitioner in the SIR writ plea, reaches SC and is seen inside the court with DK Shivakumar and Bhupesh Baghel
Supreme Court rejects PIL seeking SIT probe into vote-chori allegations
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday rejected a public interest litigation by a lawyer seeking a Special Investigation Team probe into Rahul Gandhi's allegations of anomalies in voter lists (duplicate/invalid entries, e.g. 40,000+ invalid and 10,000+ duplicates cited in Bengaluru's Mahadevapura alone). A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said a PIL in public interest would not be entertained and the petitioner is at liberty to pursue alternate remedies.

items.title: Full details of INDIA bloc's SC writ petition: 11 named petitioners, alleges ~13 crore voter deletions
items.summary: The day-3 live blog's 6:51 PM IST update names all 11 petitioners on the SIR writ petition filed ~5:16 PM IST: Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav, Saugata Roy, Tejashwi Yadav, Sanjay Raut, MA Baby, D Raja, Mahua Majhi, Supriya Sule and ET Mohammed Basheer - versus the ECI, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu. The plea alleges large-scale deletion of nearly 13 crore voters during the SIR; its contents are not yet public and the SC is expected to take it up on Tuesday.

items.title: Kharge, Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders physically file the SIR writ petition in the Supreme Court
items.summary: The day-3 live blog's 7:29 PM IST entry (with PTI visuals) shows Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders filing the petition in the Supreme Court - the in-court filing closes the day's Chalo Dilli march arc (Bhagwan Das Road stoppage -> writ petition). The plea names 11 petitioners vs the ECI, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, alleges nearly 13 crore voter deletions during the SIR; its contents are not yet public and the SC is expected to take it up on Tuesday.

The day-3 live blog's 7:50 PM IST entry reveals the contents of the 11-petitioner writ petition filed in the SC: it seeks disclosure of internal dissents among the Election Commissioners, official minutes on voter-registration (Form 6) changes, all records related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), an independent audit committee, public release of deleted voters' names with reasons, an immediate stay on the ongoing SIR process, and accountability for responsible officials. First substance of the plea that the day's Chalo Dilli march was built around; contents were not public when the filing was alerted at 7:11 AM PDT.
items.title: INDIA bloc's SIR writ petition demands revealed: interim stay on SIR, public release of deleted-voter names with reasons

items.summary: The day-3 live blog's 7:43 PM IST entry reports Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi leaving the Supreme Court after filing the petition against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Closes the day's in-court filing arc (Bhagwan Das Road stoppage -> legal team filing ~5:16 PM IST -> in-court physical filing ~7:29 PM IST). SC expected to take the plea up on Tuesday.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi leaves the Supreme Court after filing the SIR petition against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

items.source_name: thedailyjagran.com (day-3 live blog, quoting his remarks to reporters)
items.summary: Assam CM and BJP leader Himanta Biswa Sarma, speaking to reporters on the INDIA bloc's Delhi march, challenged Rahul Gandhi: ask opposition governments in Kerala, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Telangana (and the Tamil Nadu alliance government) formed during Gyanesh Kumar's tenure to resign, and announce that the opposition will not contest the upcoming Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Goa, Manipur or Uttarakhand elections (or accept any seat) if Kumar remains CEC. Escalates his earlier X attack accusing Rahul Gandhi of selectively questioning electoral outcomes.
items.title: Himanta Biswa Sarma challenges Rahul Gandhi: resign opposition state governments, boycott elections if CEC stays
Air India asks why it wasn't kept in loop before police boarded flight to detain CJP leaders; seeks BCAS protocol guidelines
items.summary: Air India has asked the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) for guidelines covering situations where police personnel enter aircraft to detain people, after Delhi Police boarded the Mumbai-Delhi flight to detain Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on Oct 10. The airline also asked why it wasn't informed of the move in advance and under what circumstances police were permitted to board the plane (The Hindu, via inshorts).

items.title: Dipke accuses Delhi Police of 'mental torture' in custody, challenges them to release the full video
items.summary: From Hingoli (Maharashtra), after reaching home for his grandmother's last rites, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke accused Delhi Police of mentally torturing him and his family during his Oct 10-11 detention. He alleged cops denied him contact with his lawyers, wouldn't let him use his phone, and did not inform his parents or lawyers of his whereabouts throughout the day. He challenged police to release the ENTIRE custody video rather than an 'edited version' — a direct rebuttal to the police-sourced footage (logged 03:56Z) showing officers informing him of his grandmother's death 'with due sensitivity'. PTI video; via thedailyjagran article updated ~12:15 PM IST Oct 12.

items.title: Dipke reacts to Jantar Mantar de-notification on X: 'Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!'
items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke posted his first X reaction to Delhi Police's de-notification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site: 'They have removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Yes, it's no longer a protest site as anyway it was turned into a war zone by the coward dictator. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!' He accused the government of restricting democratic protests and targeting the right to dissent; police designated Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as alternatives. The post is dated Oct 12 and was never logged by earlier runs (catch-up).

items.title: Keralam Assembly passes resolution seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal
items.summary: Keralam Assembly passed a resolution (moved by CM V.D. Satheesan, backed by LDF; only BJP's 3 MLAs opposed) seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's removal over alleged SIR irregularities. Three demands: rectify SIR irregularities, restore voting rights of wrongfully excluded voters, and initiate CEC removal proceedings; it also calls for reconstituting the Election Commission selection panel to comprise the PM, Leader of Opposition (Lok Sabha) and CJI. Satheesan: 'Keralam makes history' — first such resolution by the state Assembly.

items.title: Neha Bora (AISA) at the Dilli Chalo march: 'This is exactly what democracy looks like'
items.summary: AISA president Neha Bora, marching in the Dilli Chalo march to the Supreme Court, said people have not forgotten democracy: 'This is exactly what democracy looks like. Do you think that by blocking roads, closing metro stations, and cancelling trains, you can stop democracy from coming? You may forget democracy, but the people of this country who have shed their blood have not forgotten democracy, which is why we are on the streets.' ANI-wire quote carried by indianeconomicobserver.com and webindia123.com; same wire, so single-sourced. First new statement from Bora since her march participation was confirmed.

items.title: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma announces BJP rallies at every district HQ, Oct 13-31, to counter Rahul Gandhi's ECI campaign
items.summary: In Guwahati on Monday, Sarma announced peaceful BJP rallies at every district headquarters across Assam from Oct 13 to Oct 31, in direct response to Rahul Gandhi's ECI/SIR campaign and the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court. In an X post he accused Congress of mounting 'an attack on the very foundations of India's vibrant democracy' and trying to pressure constitutional institutions (including the judiciary after the CJI declined a meeting), saying democracy is valid for Congress only when it delivers it victory. He also defended the SIR as necessary against cross-border infiltration (citing Indrajit Gupta's 30-lakh stat) and called for SIR every five years.

items.title: Akhilesh Yadav: 'Changing the protest site will not save the government'
items.summary: Speaking to ANI during the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court on Monday, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav vowed the agitation would continue, accused the BJP of colluding with the Election Commission to destroy the Constitution, and demanded the EC be removed. Reacting to Jantar Mantar's de-notification as a protest site, he said changing the venue would neither save the government nor hide its 'thefts', and called for more protest venues to be provided. In the same coverage, Congress leader Sachin Pilot alleged police used force against protesters during the march (unconfirmed).

items.title: Full named list of the 11 SIR writ petitioners + detailed reliefs now published (PTI)
items.summary: PTI's Monday-evening reporting on the Supreme Court filing names all 11 petitioners for the first time: Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Saugata Roy, Akhilesh Yadav, Tejashwi Yadav, Sanjay Raut, D Raja, Mahua Majhi, MA Baby, Supriya Sule and ET Mohammed Basheer. The Article 32 plea seeks suspension of the nationwide SIR exercise pending adjudication, an independent audit committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge, production of the ECI's internal records (files, minutes, notings, dissents) on the SIR decision, and cites a report that the two Election Commissioners recorded objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months. The court is expected to take it up Tuesday.

items.title: SC clarifies on Oct 12 it never adjudicated the ECI's revised Form 6; matter listed for Oct 27
items.summary: A Supreme Court bench (CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana) clarified on Monday, October 12 that it had never adjudicated, approved or rejected the ECI's modified Form 6 declaration for new voter registration (which requires new voters to state whether they or their parents were mapped in an earlier SIR), noting the revised form did not exist when the May 2026 Bihar SIR judgment was delivered. The CJI cautioned against selectively interpreting the Court's observations ('Please don't pick words for news items'). The bench scheduled the matter, along with connected petitions concerning the Election Commission and CEC Gyanesh Kumar, for October 27. The clarification neither establishes that the form was introduced illegally nor validates the ECI's defence that the earlier judgment covers it.

items.title: 'Tale of two Nehas': police detained a lookalike at RK Ashram while the real Neha Bora reached CP
items.summary: On Sunday, AISA president Neha Bora teased on X ('Do I have your attention?... Time & Venue incoming') and announced a 2:30 PM gathering at RK Ashram. Police took into custody there a woman matching her signature look (scarf, black-rimmed glasses, mask) — actually a lookalike; Bora's sister later posted a photo with the lookalike, writing 'The tale of the two Nehas. Not strategy, just coincidence.' Meanwhile the real Bora blockaded Connaught Place ('We have crossed the barricades and reached CP') and was eventually detained at Vijay Chowk. 200+ Sunday protesters were also detained.

items.title: Neha Bora posts video alleging cramped police-bus cells; says women packed in, men 'abused and kicked'
items.summary: After her Sunday detention, AISA president Neha Bora posted a video on X describing the police bus as having four cramped cells with no room to breathe, alleging women were packed into a small compartment and male protesters were abused and kicked. Police have not responded to the claims in the reports available. Background: she had recently ended a 23-day hunger strike at the same spot; by ~2:51 PM Sunday she announced reaching Connaught Place before being taken into custody around 3 PM.

items.title: SC registry flags 14 defects in Rahul Gandhi-led SIR writ petition; must be cured before listing
items.summary: The Supreme Court registry flagged 14 defects in the INDIA bloc's SIR writ petition (diary no. 64196/2026), filed by Rahul Gandhi plus 10 other opposition leaders on Oct 12: naming individual Election Commissioners as respondents, missing vakalatnamas from nine petitioners, no copy of an earlier relevant judgment attached, an illegible ID copy of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, a Rs 220 court-fee shortfall, and font/legibility issues. Under the SC Rules 2013 the defects must be rectified before the petition can be assigned to a bench and listed for hearing; the timeline for rectification is unclear. The ECI has not publicly responded to the petition's specific allegations.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (meeting held Monday; exact time not stated)
items.title: Revanth Reddy calls anti-SIR fight 'another freedom movement', urges 'Gyanesh Go Back' / 'SIR Go Back' slogans at Delhi meeting
items.summary: Telangana CM A. Revanth Reddy, speaking Monday at Telangana Bhavan in New Delhi as part of the Congress/INDIA bloc 'Vote Bachao... Desh Bachao' (Save Vote... Save Country) campaign, said the struggle to safeguard voting rights is akin to another freedom movement — invoking the historic 'Simon Go Back' stir and urging activists to fight with 'Gyanesh Go Back' and 'SIR Go Back' slogans. Per the CMO statement, he alleged the Modi government conspired with CEC Gyanesh Kumar to delete voters' names under the guise of the SIR ('Vote chori'), said the fight is led by Kharge, Rahul Gandhi and INDIA alliance leaders, and faulted the 2023 change to EC appointments. Meeting attended by Deputy CM Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, state ministers, TPCC chief Mahesh Kumar Goud, AICC observer Sachin Sawant and MPs/MLAs/MLCs. Corroborated by IANS (hiindia, ianslive) and ANI (devdiscourse) versions of the same statement.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, daytime IST (reported ~12:13 AM IST, Oct 13)
items.title: Sarma escalates counter-front: ready for ballot-paper polls if Congress govts resign; demands SIR every 5 years; BJP Assam rallies till Oct 31
items.summary: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma at a Monday press conference in Guwahati said he is ready to contest elections via ballot paper if Rahul Gandhi gets Congress governments in Kerala, Karnataka and Telangana to resign, claiming they were formed via 'vote chori' under CEC Gyanesh Kumar; demanded Gandhi resign first since he was elected through the same process. He defended the SIR as essential to check demographic change and demanded it every five years, and announced BJP Assam will hold peaceful mass rallies at every district headquarters until Oct 31 in support of constitutional institutions. Extends his earlier alerted 'resign your governments / boycott elections' challenge with new specifics.

items.title: Himanta Biswa Sarma alleges foreign-backed 'regime change' plot behind CEC protests
items.summary: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma told reporters in Guwahati (Oct 12) that political forces, encouraged by foreign powers opposed to India's rise, were attempting a 'regime change in India without popular support' - directly tying the protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar to 'frustrated elements', the Modi govt's Naxalism crackdown, Northeast peace efforts and the military response to Pakistan. He branded domestic critics 'Dimagi Naxals'. He offered no evidence and named no powers. CATCH-UP: published ~8:56 PM IST Oct 12 (IANS), never logged by earlier runs.

After the 11-petitioner writ was filed, Rahul Gandhi posted on X thanking marchers and supporters, saying the day showed 'the people of India are not going to be intimidated' and 'We will not accept being bullied.' He asked where the 'cowards of the RSS' - who he alleged beat young protesters over the weekend - were, calling them and PM Modi 'bullies' who 'can only use power to fight.' CATCH-UP: posted ~10:26 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live key update), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi's post-march X statement: thanks supporters, calls PM Modi and RSS 'bullies'

items.summary: AAP leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh wrote to PM Narendra Modi demanding a special Parliament session 'at the earliest' to discuss alleged 'vote-chori', the deletion of 13+ crore names from voter lists, and the police crackdown on protesters demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. New parliamentary front in the agitation. CATCH-UP: letter reported ~7:49 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live), never logged by earlier runs.

items.summary: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey told ANI that Rahul Gandhi 'wants to destroy the country's constitution,' questioning the march to the Supreme Court ('Have you ever heard from 1947 until today that people go to the Supreme Court to protest?'), drawing parallels with the Emergency imposed by Indira Gandhi, and saying constitutional authorities can only be challenged via elections, no-confidence motions or impeachment. CATCH-UP: ~7:39 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey: Rahul Gandhi 'wants to destroy the Constitution', invokes Emergency

CATCH-UP: ~6:36 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: Union minister Kiren Rijiju calls Congress 'directionless', says abusing constitutional authorities 'deplorable'

items.summary: The Kerala Congress's official X handle posted 'Dear Surya Kant, if law and order is not your domain, resign now. We will find your replacement who can handle it' - then deleted it after backlash. Rijiju shared a screenshot alleging the judiciary is Congress's next target; BJP Kerala unit accused Congress of Emergency-era judiciary intimidation; the SC Bar Association condemned remarks seeking the CJI's resignation as undermining the judiciary; Congress MP Pawan Khera distanced the party, calling the post 'completely incorrect.' CATCH-UP: row broke ~7:26 PM IST Oct 12 (article updated 11:56 PM IST), never logged by earlier runs.

CATCH-UP: ~7:08 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: CPI MP P Sandosh Kumar writes to Amit Shah over alleged harassment of journalists covering protests

Ye mera vishay nahin hai' (a law-and-order issue, not my domain), declined to comment on the opposition's march to the Supreme Court, and reiterated that the court's doors are open to all. CATCH-UP: Monday Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live 04:10 PM IST), never logged by earlier runs.

CATCH-UP: ~7:42 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live), never logged by earlier runs.

items.summary: Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee, who joined the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court, told reporters the movement seeks 'justice for the sake of humanity.' CATCH-UP: ~7:32 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: Mamata Banerjee on joining the march: 'We are demanding justice for the sake of humanity'
Abhijeet Dipke posts grandmother tribute on Instagram after last rites
items.summary: First personal Instagram post from CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke since his Oct 11 release and return home to Hingoli for his grandmother's last rites: an image captioned 'The only dictator I'll happily bow down to. Grandma left every little bit of herself in you. ❤️' (~159K likes). A second captionless image post also surfaced on his account (Instagram metadata ~1:38 PM IST, Oct 12; ~61K likes) with no established facts. Instagram metadata timing has proved unreliable on this account in past runs; both posts were never reported by earlier runs. Corroboration search for a second outlet failed on a tool error, so confidence stays single-sourced. No new detentions/releases/court orders/injuries/restriction changes/new protest fronts.

items.title: CJP co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka re-detained at Jantar Mantar as the 24-hour ultimatum deadline hit
items.summary: Mathrubhumi English (IG reel, 04:22:24Z) shows on-screen text that CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka 'sneak into Jantar Mantar': two men are seen climbing over a tall black metal gate, protesters with Indian flags run onto the street, and Delhi Police in khaki move in and detain the group — 'Delhi Police detain them along with other CJP volunteers.' Independently, a News18 J&K graphic (FB post, 04:21:25Z) says that 'after breaking barricades to reach Jantar-Mantar, CJP members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were again taken into custody by police.' Lands ~9:50-9:55 AM IST, right at the 24-hour deadline for police to respond to CJP's ultimatum (~10 AM IST). No web-news coverage of this re-detention yet; note that two verified TV/news-brand social accounts posted it within a minute of each other with actual footage (not a static graphic), which is stronger than the unverified HT-graphic claim dismissed last run.

items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke's first X post on Tuesday's Jantar Mantar re-detention (Oct 13, ~9:55 AM IST): 'Cockroaches with the Tiranga sneaked into Jantar Mantar early this morning before they were picked up by Delhi Police. @AshutoshRanka, @SauravDassss, @AjinkyaCJP along with other team members have been detained. You cannot denotify the resistance, @narendramodi.' Delhi Police/ANI confirmed Das and Ranka's detention; interim leader Ajinkya Shinde's detention is named only by Dipke so far (police have not confirmed him). Article first appeared on LatestLY at 9:57 AM IST.
items.title: Dipke's first X reaction to the Tuesday re-detention: 'You cannot denotify the resistance' - names interim leader Ajinkya Shinde detained too

items.summary: The Supreme Court will NOT hear the Rahul Gandhi-led SIR writ petition (Diary 64196/2026) on Tuesday, Oct 13. The registry's 14 defects - missing vakalatnamas for 9 of the 11 petitioners, a Rs 220 court-fee shortfall, an illegible copy of Mallikarjun Kharge's ID, and individual ECs named as respondents - must be cured before the matter can be listed. The petitioners' legal team has requested the matter be listed on Wednesday, Oct 14 after the defects are cured. (Defects were flagged Oct 12; the Tuesday non-hearing + Wednesday re-list request is new, confirmed by Hindustan Times, The Bengal Today and TezzBuzz.)
items.title: SC SIR petition: Tuesday hearing off; petitioners seek Wednesday listing after curing 14 registry defects

items.summary: Dipke's first Instagram reaction to Tuesday morning's Jantar Mantar re-detention: caption 'Waiving Tiranga at Jantar Mantar! You cannot de-notify the movement, Modi!' (~55K likes). Mirrors his already-reported X statement naming Das, Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde as detained. He also posted IG stories ('Waiving the Tiranga at Jantar Mantar - Well done Cockroaches!' / 'Bravo team!').

Participant's own post corroborates the detention from the CJP side.
items.title: Ranka's own IG reel from the gate-climb: 'Fortress Jantar Mantar has been breached'

ANI wire via The Daily Jagran, APNA MA TV, Devdiscourse and GTC News.
items.title: Delhi Police registers multiple FIRs over Monday's Opposition march — barricade-breaking, graffiti alleged

items.summary: The Special Commissioner of Police (Operations) wrote to the MHA on Oct 12 asking the deployment of 273 CAPF companies in Delhi be extended from Monday till Oct 20, citing possible protests by CJP and other organisations; flagged sensitive points: Jantar Mantar, the EC, Parliament House, India Gate. 301 companies approved in all (221 on Oct 6 + 80 on Oct 8); 28 of the extra 80 had not reported by Monday; News18 cites intelligence inputs on further CJP marches.
items.title: Delhi Police seeks CAPF deployment in Delhi extended till Oct 20

items.summary: Third Tuesday petition joins the two already tracked: the Indian Youth Congress plea by president Uday Bhanu Chib against Delhi Police's Oct-1 refusal of permission to protest CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar (applied Sep 25 for 100-150 people; invokes Articles 14, 19(1)(a)-(b); challenges 'mechanical application' of protest guidelines). On Monday, Justice Amit Mahajan deferred it to Tuesday after ASG Chetan Sharma sought time to take instructions; Siddharth Luthra and Vivek Tankha appeared for IYC.
items.title: NEW legal front: Delhi HC to hear IYC's Jantar Mantar permission-denial plea Tuesday (police sought time)

WE HAVE ENTERED JANTAR MANTAR AND NOW WE ARE BEING DETAINED! ... We can do it! Gyanu, you are done bro!' His first personal statement since the ~9:52 AM IST gate-climb detention (already alerted via Mathrubhumi/News18 footage).

This is a message to the government—Hands off people’s Jantar Mantar! Gyanu’s time is over. #CockroachesReassembling.' A companion reel posted minutes earlier (~10:15 AM IST) is captioned 'Reclaiming Jantar Mantar'.
