items.title: Official CJP 'illegally kidnapped' claim post is gone from @cockroachjantaparty — deleted within ~1 hour of posting
items.summary: The official @cockroachjantaparty post (posted ~10:43 AM PDT / ~11:13 PM IST, Oct 13) claiming Ranka, Das and Shinde were 'illegally kidnapped' for 14+ hours and calling Delhi Police 'puppets of the government' is no longer on the handle. It was live and alerted at ~10:49 AM PDT (~19K likes within minutes); by ~11:52 AM PDT a direct post lookup returns 'Could not load post on any platform' and a sweep of 928 posts on the account finds no trace of it. Whether CJP pulled it or Instagram removed it is unclear — Instagram is currently restricting protest-related accounts at scale (MediaNama: 200+ Sahyog takedown orders ahead of Oct 10; IFF says ~20 accounts taken down/restricted). No re-post or explanation from the handle yet. Watch for a repost or official explanation.
items.source_name: Instagram (official handle, verified via instagram-cli direct lookup)

items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke publicly challenged CJI Surya Kant over remarks attributed to the CJI that law-and-order matters were outside his domain, asking: 'Will you tell Modi the same thing?' The quip, made on Tuesday, adds a direct political edge to the debate over the judiciary's response to the Delhi protest crackdown and SIR dispute — days after Congress Kerala's similar 'not your domain' post drew a contempt complaint. Corroborating outlets: Hindustan Times (Arya Mishra), Kashmir Post.
items.title: 'Will you tell Modi the same thing?': Dipke publicly challenges CJI Surya Kant over 'law and order not my domain' remark
Founder Dipke's birthday tribute to detained co-convener Ashutosh Ranka
items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke posted on Instagram @abhijeetdipke (2:40 PM PDT / 8:10 PM IST Oct 13, ~5.3K likes): a birthday tribute to CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka, 'spending your birthday in detention' — recalling the Oct 10 detention and court appearance ('We will do whatever you decide') and writing 'they can detain a person, but they can never detain the courage and conviction that person carries.' Confirms Ranka still in detention at Jaffarpur Kalan on Oct 13 evening. First logged post from the founder since his return to Hingoli; no new facts beyond the continued-detention confirmation and the tribute itself.

items.title: DK Shivakumar: 'no double standards' after Bengaluru police detained anti-SIR/CEC protesters
items.summary: Bengaluru police detained and removed a group of anti-SIR/CEC protesters near K.R. Circle on Oct 12 after they gathered without permission to march toward the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer's office. In a Tuesday press briefing, Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar said the right to peaceful protest is fundamental: 'we cannot demand the right to protest in Delhi and deny it in Bengaluru' — he sought a full report on the police action and said any unnecessary force or excess will bring accountability ('accountability will follow'). Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge added Tuesday morning that the police handling would be reviewed and ordered that no peaceful demonstration be disrupted. First tracked Bengaluru-police-action episode with a top-state-level political response.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 13 (Tuesday court hearing; order pronounced during the day)
items.title: CORRECTION: NSUI outsiders-assault plea's next hearing is Friday Oct 16, not November — Centre gets 3 weeks for maintainability objections
items.summary: Correcting this watch's earlier 'adjourned to November' dating of the NSUI outsiders-assault PIL: Tuesday's Delhi HC hearing (bench: Acting CJ Nitin Wasudeo Sambre + Justice Sanjay Sharma) on NSUI national president Vinod Jakhar's plea for an SIT probe into alleged Oct-10 assaults on protesters by 'outsiders' at Connaught Place and adjoining roads ended with the court permitting ASG Chetan Sharma to file preliminary objections to maintainability under PIL Rules 9(f)/9(g) within three weeks — and listing the matter next on Friday, October 16. The court also asked the petitioner to produce copies of related Supreme Court petitions to check overlap, and directed the ASG's objection affidavit on record. Counsel additionally sought preservation of CCTV footage from the protest site and clarification on alleged house arrests. (November date appears to have been conflated with the IYC plea's Nov-17 listing.)

items.title: Pregnant journalist alleges Rahul Gandhi pushed her during Oct 12 INDIA-bloc march; BJP amplifies, Congress denies
items.summary: Oneindia journalist Richa Parashar, who says she is 3 months pregnant, alleges Rahul Gandhi grabbed her hand and pulled her as she covered the Oct 12 INDIA-bloc march near the Supreme Court; she says she fell on the steps (hurting hand/knees, breaking her phone) and her cameraperson fell on top of her. She was admitted to hospital. BJP leaders Pradeep Bhandari, Rajesh Bhatia and Umang Bajaj visited her in hospital; Bhandari alleged Gandhi 'shoved and pushed her to the ground'. Congress MP Pawan Khera called the claims 'completely false'; Jebi Mather accused the BJP of 'scripting narratives'. Key facts remain unverified.

items.title: Delhi Police moved detained leaders Ranka, Das (and others) out of Jaffarpur Kalan PS ~2:30 AM; destination unknown
items.summary: Nighttime transfer: Delhi Police escorted CJP leaders including Ashutosh Ranka and Sourav Das out of the Jaffarpur Kalan police station at ~2:30 AM and loaded them into a white tourist van as a crowd filmed; on-screen text asks where police took them. Both The Lallantop's on-the-ground team and the MaatiTak reel independently captured the 2 AM move. Whereabouts now unknown — watch for release vs transfer/production before magistrate.
items.source_name: MaatiTak (@officialmaatitak) IG reel; corroborated by The Lallantop (India Today Group) ground report

items.title: Detained trio under 'preventive arrest', to be produced in court today; Ratna Singh names charges including bond violation — Tihar judicial custody possible
items.summary: Multiple outlets (NDTV, News18 India, SAAM TV, Sun News Tamil, Mathrubhumi News, Times Now) citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh report Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde are under preventive arrest over the Tue-AM Jantar Mantar gate-climb/Tricolour-hoisting and will be produced before a court on Wednesday, Oct 14. Named charges: trespass, violation of the Oct-11 one-year peace bond, obstruction of a public official's duty. NDTV cites Ratna Singh's post saying the three could be sent to judicial custody in Tihar Jail. News18's graphics add the police allegation that the protesters broke open the door of the JDU office to enter the protest site. Overnight, Ratna Singh told reporters (MaatiTak night statement) protesters were held nearly 24 hours without lawyer access or stated grounds, alleging Delhi Police acted 'on orders from above'. The official @cockroachjantaparty 'kidnapped' claim post from Oct 13 was earlier deleted from the handle.
items.source_name: NDTV / News18 India / SAAM TV / Sun News Tamil / Mathrubhumi News / Times Now (via Instagram), citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh

items.title: Overnight whereabouts resolved: detained trio brought to Parliament Street PS ~3 AM; SEM production at Mandir Marg expected — outcome still unreported
items.summary: CJP legal head Ratna Singh's overnight X posts (livemint; corroborated by thedailyjagran and Latestly) resolve the 'destination unknown' open question: Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde were brought to Parliament Street Police Station at ~3 AM IST Oct 14 in a private van, after the ~2:30 AM move out of Jaffarpur Kalan PS; they were held nearly 24 hours without lawyer access or stated grounds. Singh's 5:38 AM IST update said the trio are likely to be produced before the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) at Mandir Marg Police Station within an hour (due ~6:30-7:00 AM IST); the production outcome is still unreported as of this run. Delhi Police's position remains 'preventive arrest' (ANI); Singh calls the arrests illegal and says Tihar judicial custody is possible.
items.source_name: livemint (HT Media); corroborated by thedailyjagran (Jagran Prakashan) and Latestly — all citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh's X posts

items.title: CJP trio sent to 5 days' judicial custody after SEM Mandir Marg production
items.summary: SAAM TV (verified @saamtvnews, 3.1M followers) live Marathi BIG BREAKING segment at ~9:00 AM IST Oct 14: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde sent to 5 days' jail ('CJP netyanna 5 divasancha turungvas'); the segment shows a spokesperson criticizing the Modi government for jailing the activists, calling the arrests politically motivated suppression of dissent. Within the same minute, VOB News Network (@vob.network) posted a Hindi 'BREAKING NEWS' graphic: three CJP leaders sent to 5 days of judicial custody — naming Sourav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde (spellings rendered 'Tanka'/'Animesh' in the graphic); charges: entering Jantar Mantar without permission, obstructing government work, violating bond conditions; notes the Oct-10 detention and Jantar Mantar's de-notification; Tihar Jail named. This is the long-awaited outcome of Ratna Singh's 5:38 AM IST 'SEM Mandir Marg within one hour' post — production landed ~2-3h late, ~9:00 AM IST. Caveat: as of ~9:08 AM IST no mainstream web outlet has yet carried the custody outcome; both sources are IG video/graphic news posts.

items.title: Dipke's first response to the 5-day custody order: dares Modi to 'declare an Emergency'
items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke issued his first reaction to the SEM Mandir Marg custody order via his verified X account @abhijeet_dipke (post dated 8:50 AM IST, Oct 14; screenshot reposted to his IG @abhijeetdipke with caption 'Coward.', ~13.6K likes). He says 'Ashu' and 'Saurav' were sent to 5 days' judicial custody for 'unfurling tricolour at Jantar Mantar,' and directly challenges PM Narendra Modi to 'show some guts' and officially declare an Emergency instead of using 'cowardly tactics' to crush dissent. Note: his post names only Das and Ranka (2 of the 3) — Shinde's custody status rests on the SAAM TV/VOB graphics alone. Self-published leader statement; no second outlet yet covering the post itself.

items.event_time_ist: ~9:00 AM IST, Oct 14 (correction surfaced ~9:21 AM IST, Oct 14)
items.title: Correction: only Das and Ranka got 5-day judicial custody — Ajinkya Shinde released on personal bond
items.summary: LiveLaw (published 9:01 AM IST, updated 9:07 AM IST Oct 14) reports the SEM court's custody order in the Oct-13 Jantar Mantar 'trespass' case: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka remanded to 5 days' judicial custody; Ajinkya Shinde was released on personal bond — NOT sent to Tihar. This corrects the earlier ~9:00 AM IST alert, which relied on early IG news graphics (SAAM TV, VOB) that described all three leaders as getting 5-day judicial custody. Two other categories independently report the same split outcome: Bar & Bench's 03:51:14Z 'BREAKING NEWS' IG graphic headlines only Das and Ranka being sent to 5-day judicial custody, and India Today's live stream is titled 'CJP Leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka Sent To Tihar Jail' — neither names Shinde for custody. Context: FIR for alleged trespass/unlawful assembly/disobedience after Jantar Mantar's de-notification; trio detained Tue AM, held at Jaffarpur Kalan, moved to Parliament Street ~3 AM, produced at SEM Mandir Marg this morning.

Official @cockroachjantaparty image post (posted 20:57 UTC Oct 13 / ~2:27 AM IST Oct 14, post_id 18013549097972581): 'First in Ashutosh and Saurav's bloodline to be jailed for unfurling India's national flag. If we don't rise up against this crackdown on dissent, we will lose our country to Modi and Shah's dictatorship - Emergency 2.0 is here because we started Jantar Mantar 2.0.' Catch-up: this official statement's text was never logged by any earlier run - this run's IG-CLI leg surfaced it. Lands hours before Wednesday's SEM Mandir Marg order sending Das and Ranka to 5-day judicial custody.
items.title: CJP official handle: Das/Ranka 'jailed for unfurling the national flag', warns of 'Emergency 2.0'
Dipke demands Ranka and Das's release in overnight IG reel
items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke posted a video reel on Instagram at ~3:48 AM IST, Oct 14 captioned 'Release Ashu & Saurav now!' — a release demand for co-conveners Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das while they were in detention custody (before the 5-day judicial-custody order was passed later that morning). The reel never surfaced in any earlier check.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 14 (Wednesday morning; exact X post time unconfirmed)
items.summary: Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi posted on X on Wednesday condemning the 5-day judicial custody of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka: 'Waving the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar in a peaceful protest is not a crime. Jailing youth for it is an act of cowardice. Students. Youth. Journalists. The INDIA bloc. Different banners, one cause. All protests are one: citizens demanding their constitutional rights.' He added: 'Jantar Mantar belongs to the people of India. We will reclaim it.' AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal also condemned the arrests on X: 'Is waving our own flag in our own country a crime? This is absolutely ridiculous.'
items.title: Rahul Gandhi backs CJP on X: waving the Tricolour 'not a crime', jailing youth 'an act of cowardice'

items.summary: In an ANI video statement (his first on-camera response after the JC order), CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said CJP shares the same cause as the INDIA bloc's anti-SIR agitation but will remain an independent pressure group and never merge with a political party. He accused the government of imposing an 'unofficial Emergency' — 'Even during the actual Emergency, things didn't go this far' — and dared PM Modi to declare one officially. He rejected 'Urban Naxalism' allegations against the movement ('If you are in power and want to investigate, then go ahead and investigate'). Ajinkya Shinde said CJP's National Working Committee would meet to decide the next course of action; AAP's Saurabh Bhardwaj called the custody order 'DICTATORSHIP' on X.
items.title: Dipke's first video statement after JC order: 'unofficial Emergency' charge, rejects 'Urban Naxalism' tag

items.summary: Delhi Police's Wednesday statement says Das, Ranka and Shinde were arrested under preventive provisions citing alleged repeated attempts to disturb public peace, violate the law, and instigate others through social media. Police detail the Oct 13 morning incident: the three plus 11 CJP members entered the denotified Jantar Mantar via private premises; all 14 detained; two FIRs registered (No. 289/26 at Connaught Place PS under BNSS secs 223(a), 332, 61(2); No. 128/26 at Parliament Street PS under 221, 115(2), 132, 121(1), 3(5)). Produced before the SEM Mandir Marg under BNSS 126/170; Das and Ranka remanded to 5 days' JC on apprehension they would repeat violations and instigate others if bailed; Shinde bound down for SIX MONTHS to maintain peace on personal bond + Rs 5,000 surety. Dipke's first reaction: 'Since when has hoisting the Tricolour become such a grave sin...?' — accuses the govt of an 'unofficial Emergency'. AAP leader Saurabh Bhardwaj called the remand 'DICTATORSHIP' on X; defense counsel Abhisht Hela questioned the legal basis of the preventive action, alleging suppression of dissent.
items.title: Delhi Police releases official statement on CJP arrests: cites social-media instigation; FIR numbers, Shinde's 6-month bind-down revealed

items.summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi has moved the Supreme Court challenging the manner in which the Election Commission is conducting the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Advocate Nizamuddin Pasha mentioned the plea on Wednesday before a CJI Surya Kant-led bench, seeking that it be heard alongside the connected SIR matters listed for Thursday, October 15. The CJI said he would check and list it with the similar cases. The petition joins the Oct-12 writ plea by Rahul Gandhi and 10 INDIA bloc leaders and other pending SIR challenges; specific grounds and reliefs were not detailed at mentioning.
items.title: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi moves Supreme Court challenging SIR of electoral rolls

items.summary: PTI's verified multimedia account published footage of CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke arriving in Delhi (airport terminal), fulfilling his Oct-13 pledge from Hingoli to reach the capital on Wednesday. Surrounded by reporters (NDTV, PTI mics) and uniformed police, he gives his first on-camera statement since the SEM Mandir Marg order: Ashu and Saurav were sent to five days' jail for unfurling the tricolour at Jantar Mantar — "Is waving the tricolour wrong? This is a sign of dictatorship." Single-sourced to the PTI reel as of this run (no web-news outlet carrying the arrival yet); the watch had Dipke in Hingoli as its top watch item.
items.title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke arrives in Delhi from Hingoli; first on-camera statement since 5-day JC order

items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke spoke to reporters in Delhi (The Hindu video posted ~4:37 PM IST Oct 14) — his first on-camera appearance since arriving from Hingoli this afternoon. He addressed BJP leader Piyush Goyal's Tuesday allegation that Congress bribed former CECs with Padma awards and posts; challenged lawyer Harish Salve and Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis to produce evidence for their foreign-funding claims and hand it to Home Minister Amit Shah; and argued that hoisting the Tricolour cannot be treated as a peace-bond violation, invoking the Constitution, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, and voting rights.
items.title: Dipke's first Delhi press scrum since arrival: answers Goyal's Padma-bribe charge, challenges Salve and Fadnavis on foreign-funding evidence

items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke announced a fresh protest in an X video message (Wednesday morning): a 'Lehra Do Tiranga' Tiranga march at Central Park, Connaught Place, Delhi, on October 16 at 5 PM, protesting the 5-day judicial custody of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Supporters were urged to bring the tricolour; those unable to reach Delhi were asked to organise Tiranga marches in their own cities. Dipke declared he is 'not afraid of jails' / 'ready to go to jail.'
items.title: Dipke calls fresh 'Lehra Do Tiranga' protest at Delhi's Connaught Place on Oct 16, 5 PM

items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke announced that the 11 party volunteers detained by Delhi Police in Tuesday's (Oct-13) Jantar Mantar gate-entry incident have been released ('Spirits unbroken, waving the tricolour the moment they walked free'), calling their arrest illegal. Independently corroborated: Livemint reports (byline, Garvit Bhirani) that CJP legal head Ratna Singh credited advocate Abhisht Hela's legal team with 'securing the release of Ajinkya Shinde and 11 other volunteers detained by Delhi Police'. Ajinkya Shinde himself was released on a personal bond; Das and Ranka remain in 5-day judicial custody at Tihar.
items.title: RELEASE — 11 CJP volunteers freed from Oct-13 Jantar Mantar detention

items.summary: Judicial Magistrate First Class Rahul Jain of Saket Courts issued fresh dasti summons to YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in the 2018 defamation case (Vikas Sankrityayan @ Vikas Pandey vs Dhruv Rathee, Ct. Cases 5786/2018). Complainant sought preponement of the Nov-20 listing arguing Rathee, who ordinarily lives abroad, is presently in India with respect to the 'CJP protest' and that service had been delayed for years. Next hearing: October 17.
items.title: Saket Court issues fresh summons to Dhruv Rathee in 2018 defamation case, citing his presence in India for the CJP protest; hearing on Oct 17

items.summary: Supreme Court Advocate-on-Record Amita Sachdeva filed a civil defamation suit against Dhruv Rathee at Delhi's Saket Court over his video claiming Lord Ram and Sita ate meat and drank alcohol during exile. She seeks a formal declaration, an injunction against similar videos, and damages, arguing a citizen's religious identity forms part of their legal character. District Judge Mohinder Virat heard submissions; next hearing: November 5.
items.title: Defamation suit filed against Dhruv Rathee at Saket Court over Ram-Sita video; next hearing Nov 5

items.source_name: LatestLY (original byline); Millben allegation via IANS wire
items.summary: American singer and vocal Modi supporter Mary Millben alleged on X (Oct 14) that CJP is being funded by US-based donors opposed to PM Narendra Modi, and urged Indian youth to 'rise up' and organize peaceful counter-protests against the party. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke rejected the claim on X, asking 'Why is Modi seeking the support of Americans to discredit his own countrymen?' and 'We are more than capable of dealing with our own issues.' The funding allegation has no evidence provided and is not independently established; the Millben leg moved on IANS wire (hiindia, andhravilas) with original digital reporting from mtimes, kokthum and neherald, and Dipke's rebuttal was reported by LatestLY with a direct link to his X post. This opens a new counter-protest narrative around the Oct-16 Tiranga-march buildup.
items.title: Mary Millben alleges US donors fund CJP, calls for youth counter-protests; Dipke rejects claim on X
Amnesty International demands immediate release of CJP leaders, condemns Jantar Mantar denotification
items.summary: Amnesty International issued a formal press release on Oct 14 (published 9:37 PM IST) calling on Delhi authorities to immediately release CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, remanded to five days' judicial custody after trying to protest at Jantar Mantar. Amnesty International India board chair Aakar Patel said denotifying established protest sites and arresting people who use them shows 'strong authoritarian tendencies' and leaves the right to protest 'hollowed out in practice'. The statement also flags detentions of protesters travelling from Gujarat and Maharashtra and alleged mistreatment of journalists covering the protests. Maktoob Media covered the statement on Oct 15: 'Amnesty demands release of CJP leaders, says Jantar Mantar closure hollows out right to protest.' Catch-up: published before the pause baseline but never logged by earlier runs.

items.title: Dipke marks 'Day 3' of Das and Ranka's detention, calls it an 'illegal arrest' for waving the national flag
items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke posted on X on Oct 15: 'It's Day 3 of Ashu and Saurav's illegal arrest. Two young men who gave up their comfortable lives to fight for change are now languishing in jail. Imagine being jailed in your own country for waving your own national flag.' Delhi Police's stated position remains that the Oct-13 Jantar Mantar entry was trespass, breach of the Oct-11 peace bond, and repeated attempts to disturb public peace.

items.title: CJP's official Instagram reposts Oct-10 video, alleges takedown ('Dictator Modi deleted this video from October 10, so here it is again')
items.summary: The official @cockroachjantaparty account posted an Instagram story (~2:17 AM IST Oct 15) re-uploading a video from October 10 with the caption 'Dictator Modi deleted this video from October 10, so here it is again'. The takedown allegation itself is unverified; the republication is a new official-party communication.

The Supreme Court hears today (Oct 15) the full bundle of petitions arising from the CJP protest crackdown, listed at 10:30 AM IST before CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi: Rahul Gandhi and nine other INDIA bloc leaders' SIR writ petition (W.P.(C) No. 001351/2026) against the ECI's electoral-roll revision; AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi's SIR plea (alerted Oct 14); contempt petitions over the Oct-10 metro/train/internet curbs; SCBA and SCAORA petitions over alleged detention/manhandling of lawyers; journalist organisations' petitions (Free Speech Collective, Network of Women in Media, Delhi Union of Journalists) alleging assault/detention of reporters; Menaka Guruswamy's habeas corpus plea naming detained leaders including Arvind Kejriwal and Mamata Banerjee; a challenge to the constitutional validity of BNSS Section 172; and Swaty Singh's challenge to the Jantar Mantar denotification. BarandBench counts 18 petitions in all. Also on Tuesday the Court had sought the personal presence of a senior Delhi Police officer to explain the alleged assault on women journalists.
items.title: Supreme Court hearing day: ~18 petitions listed today (Oct 15) before CJI bench — Rahul Gandhi SIR writ plea, Owaisi plea, crackdown/journalist/lawyer petitions

items.summary: Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar filed a fresh affidavit in the Supreme Court on Thursday defending the Oct-10 restrictions, saying permission for the CJP's Jantar Mantar protest was denied because of the group's record: the July 20 CJP protest drew 30,000+ people including persons with rioting/rape/murder records who attacked police with stones and sticks in 'mob violence and lynching'-like scenes; the Oct 6-8 marches choked central Delhi; the NEET protest overstayed permissions by 36+ days; the Sansad Chalo march proceeded despite Sec 163 BNSS orders; injuries to over a dozen police personnel; and detained protesters punctured the tyres of the buses holding them and smashed window shields. Separately, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan tendered an 'unconditional apology' to the Court over the Oct-10 mobile-internet suspension, while denying wilful non-compliance (said it was needed to stop rumour-spreading); Railway Board chairman Satish Kumar said train curbs were imposed after review to maintain public order; DMRC told the Court metro service was restored from 10 PM on Oct 10 per the Court's order (45 stations had been shut 9 PM Oct 9 to 6 PM Oct 10). One outlet (newspop.in) reports 7,000+ people were detained across Delhi during the operation — single-sourced.
items.title: Delhi Police Commissioner files affidavit in SC defending Oct-10 curbs (cites July 20 violence, police injuries, bus vandalism); Union Home Secretary tenders 'unconditional apology' over internet ban

items.summary: Four advocates (petition filed by Divyansh Bisht, mentioned by Senior Advocate Gaurav Bhatia) have moved the Supreme Court seeking a uniform framework banning political demonstrations inside court premises and regulating protests near the SC/High Courts, plus consideration of criminal contempt proceedings against Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav and TMC MP Mahua Moitra over the Oct-12 'March for Democracy' toward the Court registry. The plea seeks preservation of CCTV footage, visitor registers, access-control records and security reports from Oct 12, and asks the Court to examine whether leaders' conduct interfered with the administration of justice. Listed for hearing today (Oct 15) before CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi.
items.title: Advocates' plea in SC seeks ban on political protests inside court premises, criminal-contempt consideration vs Rahul Gandhi, Kharge, Akhilesh, Mahua Moitra over Oct-12 march

items.summary: A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice to the Election Commission of India, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on the SIR writ petition W.P.(C) 001351/2026 filed Oct 12 by Rahul Gandhi and 12 other INDIA-bloc leaders (Kharge, Saugata Roy, Akhilesh Yadav, Tejashwi Yadav, Sanjay Raut, MA Baby, D Raja, Mahua Majhi, Supriya Sule, ET Mohammed Basheer, plus Thol. Thirumavalavan and Sajjad Kichloo who joined later). The plea challenges voter deletions and SIR irregularities and seeks ECI files, minutes, notings and ECINET/ERONET records. The court tagged it with pending SIR matters and made it returnable October 27.
items.title: SC issues notice to ECI on INDIA-bloc SIR writ; returnable Oct 27

items.summary: While entertaining the INDIA-bloc petition, the CJI-led bench ordered that the petition 'on behalf of Petitioner No. 6' (Shiv Sena-UBT MP Sanjay Raut) is entertained on a provisional basis, subject to his explaining his conduct. Raut had alleged the CJI and judges played badminton in London with BJP leaders and attended dinners with BJP ministers while declining a meeting with Rahul Gandhi. Attorney General R. Venkataramani had granted consent on Oct 14 to the Supreme Court Bar Association to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against Raut, calling the badminton claim false (citing a Delhi HC order) and the remarks scandalous. The CJI remarked the judges are 'not sitting in ivory towers' and are aware of statements made outside the courtroom.
items.title: SC asks Sanjay Raut to explain remarks against CJI, judges; AG cleared contempt route

items.summary: Other outcomes from the Oct-15 hearing before CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi: (1) Notice issued on the four-advocates' plea seeking safeguards against political demonstrations at court premises after the Oct-12 INDIA-bloc march; CJI: 'nobody can browbeat us'; Justice Bagchi ordered preservation of CCTV and digital footage of the march; an allegation that Rahul Gandhi pushed a woman journalist was raised by Gaurav Bhatia. (2) Notice issued on the challenge to BNSS Section 172, which the bench described as 'a preventive detention provision'; nodal counsel to identify overlapping issues. (3) Protection for a woman journalist and backing for a women-led panel on Delhi protest complaints (NWMI/Indira Jaising, Free Speech Collective contempt plea, Kerala Union of Working Journalists Article 32 plea). (4) The bench declined to take cognizance of the authorities' 'unqualified apology', with Justice Bagchi noting the SG's submissions made it a qualified apology. (5) The court agreed to examine a separate plea challenging the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a protest site.
items.title: SC Oct-15 hearing: notice on Oct-12 march plea, Sec 172 BNSS notice, journalist protections

items.event_time_ist: Oct 15 (orders and HC hearing); march today 5 PM IST, Oct 16
items.summary: Ahead of today's 5 PM 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Connaught Place's Central Park: NDMC closed Central Park to the public on Oct 16-17 for 'administrative reasons'; Delhi Police imposed Section 163 BNSS in CP and asked the public to stay away, offering only a select 'group of 11' at an alternate location for flag-waving and the anthem; DCP PRO Neha Yadav cited traders' letters seeking protection; traders/vendors warned of a counter-protest if they lose another festive-season weekend. The Delhi High Court on Thursday (Acting CJ Nitin Wasudeo Sambre + Justice Sanjay Sharma) refused to restrain CJP/Dipke from protesting, taking on record the police's assurance (ASG Chetan Sharma) that all regulatory steps would be taken. Delhi Police told the HC the Jantar Mantar denotification was on the Supreme Court's directions and the court suggested spacious alternative venues (The Hindu). Deployment: 6,000 Delhi Police + 220 CAPF companies + expanded CCTV; traffic advisory restricts 20 roads around CP from 3 PM. AAP has extended support and is mobilising for the march.
items.title: Tiranga march eve: NDMC shuts Central Park 2 days, Sec 163 in CP, HC refuses to restrain protest

items.summary: At a Thursday press conference, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged that vehicles without number plates are following him and Intelligence Bureau officials are monitoring his residence, and said Delhi Police could detain him Thursday night or Friday morning ahead of the Tiranga march. 'If we have to go to jail to wave the Tiranga in this country, then we are ready for it,' he said, adding: 'If we announce 100 places, will Narendra Modi shut down all 100 places?' In Friday's live coverage he asked, 'Why is PM Modi locking down Delhi to shield one individual?' Aaj Tak's graphic quoted him saying 'Police can take me into custody.' The surveillance claims are his own allegations, not independently corroborated.
items.title: Dipke alleges IB surveillance ahead of Tiranga march, says 'ready to go to jail'

items.summary: At a Thursday press conference, the Cockroach Janta Party announced a nationwide mobilisation campaign against the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls starting October 23. The party said it would take its campaign directly to states with upcoming elections to collect evidence of alleged voter-list irregularities, reiterated its demand for CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal, and said farmers, Dalits, students and Gen Z youth would participate. The party also said it has already submitted evidence to the panel hearing the SIR-related case.
items.title: CJP announces nationwide SIR campaign from Oct 23
SC declines urgent hearing on plea against NDMC's Central Park closure; "hope better sense will prevail"
items.summary: A Supreme Court bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi on Friday (Oct 16) declined to urgently hear a plea challenging the NDMC's order shutting down Central Park in Connaught Place over the Cockroach Janta Party's proposed 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march. During a mentioning by Adv Jai Anant Dehadrai flagging apprehended losses to traders from the protest, the CJI said "We hope better sense will prevail on everyone. Small shopkeepers earn their livelihood during these days." Justice Bagchi observed the protest, 'mungfali' vending and law-and-order concerns were interconnected and warned the court could exercise its constitutional powers if business losses resulted. The plea may be listed Oct 26/27. No urgent restraint on the 5 PM Tiranga march; Delhi Police have offered to facilitate a symbolic flag-waving event with 11 people.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 16, 2026 (Chidambaram's X post; ECI directive issued Oct 15)
items.summary: The Election Commission on Oct 15 issued a 15-page directive ordering a Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls — not SIR — across 17 states/UTs (incl. UP, Punjab, Bihar, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala), with Jan 1, 2027 as qualifying date, draft rolls Nov 12, final rolls Jan 4, 2027, and 'stricter scrutiny of deletions'; schedules for states where SIR is underway/completed (incl. Delhi, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Odisha) come separately. Congress leader P. Chidambaram reacted on X Oct 16: 'After the protests and the notice issued by the Supreme Court, wisdom has dawned on the ECI and Mr. Gyanesh Kumar. S.I.R. has been abandoned for the 17 remaining States and UTs' — asked why 20 states had 13.3 crore names removed 'without due process' and said 'Mr. Gyanesh Kumar should be surcharged for the double expenditure'.
items.title: ECI orders SSR (not SIR) for 17 states/UTs; Chidambaram demands Gyanesh Kumar be 'surcharged' for botched rollout

items.summary: The All India Students' Federation (AISF) and All India Youth Federation (AIYF) took out a 'Tiranga march' through Connaught Place on Thursday Oct 15 — the sixth straight day of Delhi protests — from PVR Plaza toward Central Park amid rainfall, waving tricolours and raising slogans against SIR, demanding the rollback of SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, and restoration of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. The youth organisations say around 100 protesters, including women, were detained after police stopped the march with barricades and put detainees in police vehicles; Delhi Police released no official detention figure. One participant alleged manhandling of protesters including women — unconfirmed.
items.title: AISF/AIYF 'Tiranga march' through Connaught Place on Oct 15; ~100 detained, say organisers

items.summary: A Tiranga rally was held at Azad Maidan, Mumbai on Oct 16: young demonstrators waved Indian flags and chanted 'Inquilab Zindabad'/'Jai Hind', with placards opposing EVMs and demanding cancellation of SIR; a large AISA banner identified the organizers. A live blog noted Mumbai police had permitted CJP's 'Lehra Do Tiranga' demonstration at Azad Maidan (permission detail single-sourced via trendkia). No violence depicted. This is the first protest-front outside Delhi in this arc.
items.title: Tiranga rally held at Mumbai's Azad Maidan (Oct 16) — first protest front outside Delhi
Delhi Police reaches Dipke's Delhi residence ahead of 5 PM Tiranga march
items.summary: Delhi Police personnel reached the Delhi residence where CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke is staying, about three hours before today's 5 PM 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Central Park, Connaught Place. NDTV India's breaking reel aired visuals of multiple uniformed police officers gathered outside the residential street with vehicles parked nearby. Aaj Tak's graphic identifies the residence as that of an associate (Anish Gavande) where Dipke is staying. The visit follows Dipke's Thursday claim that police/IB were monitoring his residence and his statement that he was 'ready to go to jail' for waving the national flag. No official Delhi Police statement on the visit or any detention yet; Dipke himself has not confirmed the visit publicly.

items.source_name: Daily Jagran (live blog) / BBC News India / India Today / Inshorts / Kashmir In Focus
items.summary: Escalation from the earlier police visit (~2:10 PM IST): Delhi Police served CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke a written notice at NCP-SCP spokesperson Anish Gawande's residence, where he is staying. The notice states Section 163 BNSS is in effect in Connaught Place and that NDMC gave no permission for the 5 PM 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march — a breach would be a Section 163 violation inviting legal action. Inshorts reports the notice bars him from holding the Tiranga march in Connaught Place this evening. Dipke signed/received the document (India Today: exact terms unconfirmed) and released a video statement, carried by BBC News India, saying 7–8 officers accused him of 'unlawful activities and inciting people' and told him he 'cannot go wave the tricolour,' expressing dismay at being prevented from raising the national flag in his own country. No detention has been confirmed; the 5 PM march remains called.
items.title: Delhi Police serves Abhijeet Dipke a written notice barring the Tiranga march; Dipke records video response

items.summary: AAP workers and supporters staged a 'Tiranga Rally' in the national capital today, Oct 16, directing their agitation against the Election Commission over alleged institutional irregularities in the SIR. AAP Delhi chief Saurabh Bharadwaj, holding the national flag, told ANI it was 'sheer madness' to bar Indians from unfurling the Tricolour and said the rally was being held 'right in front of the Rashtrapati Bhavan'. He questioned the massive security deployment ('50,000 security personnel... to stop the Tricolour') and the Central Park closure, rebutted BJP charges that the protests are a conspiracy to incite anarchy, and stressed the rally would be 'completely peaceful - in Mahatma Gandhi's way'. An Indian Express video shows the rally carrying a 200-ft Tiranga. Separately, AAP leader Gopal Rai backed the 'Tiranga Lahra Do' call on X and urged cadres to join the flag movement. No detentions reported from the AAP rally as of report time.
items.title: AAP stages 'Tiranga Rally' near Rashtrapati Bhavan ahead of CJP's 5 PM march
SC lists on Oct 26 journalist's plea alleging Rahul Gandhi pushed her during Oct-12 march
items.summary: The Supreme Court (CJI Surya Kant + Justice Joymalya Bagchi) agreed on Friday to list on Oct 26 an interlocutory application by journalist Richa Parashar alleging Rahul Gandhi grabbed and pulled her while she covered the Oct-12 opposition march to the SC registry, and that his security then pushed her, leaving her fallen and later hospitalised. The Congress denies the claim. Sr Adv Gaurav Bhatia mentioned the application in advocate Digant Mishra's petition seeking guidelines on demonstrations within court premises; the CJI also confirmed that notice has been issued in all connected matters.

items.title: DCP Sachin Sharma warns of legal action if 5 PM Tiranga march defies Sec 163
items.summary: DCP New Delhi Sachin Sharma urged protesters to abide by the law ahead of CJP's 5 PM 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Connaught Place, saying Abhijeet Dipke has been informed that Sec 163 BNSS is in force in the New Delhi district and has been made aware of its implications, including during the festive season; he added that police will take 'whatever legal action is appropriate' against violations.

The Daily Jagran live blog reports people have started gathering around Central Park ahead of the scheduled 5 PM 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march, despite the NDMC closure and the Sec 163 BNSS police notice. At ~4:27 PM, Abhijeet Dipke released a video message addressed to PM Modi after being served the police notice (full contents not yet detailed by outlets). The march begins in minutes under heavy deployment (6,000+ police, 220 CAPF companies).
items.title: Build-up: people gathering around Central Park; Dipke issues video message to PM Modi after police notice

items.summary: Catch-up: Mumbai Police/FRRO served actor Imran Khan (US citizen, OCI cardholder) a Leave India Notice directing him to leave India by Oct 28 for violating the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025 by joining the Oct 10 August Kranti Maidan anti-CEC protest (CJP-linked), after a complaint by BJP's Kirit Somaiya. Opposition leaders Sanjay Raut ('government is scared') and Supriya Sule ('everyone has the right to protest') slammed the move. Corroborated across Reuters (international), LawBeat and Maktoob (independent digital), and Hindustan Times (mainstream print).
items.title: Mumbai Police/FRRO order actor Imran Khan to leave India by Oct 28 over anti-CEC protest; Raut, Sule slam move

items.summary: Catch-up: CJI Surya Kant's bench declined to list a new Maharashtra SIR challenge (alleging ~33% of voters deleted, over 1 crore struck off on 'logical discrepancy'; Sr Adv Arvind Datar cited 9.79 cr voters, ~2 cr struck off, 1.22 cr flagged) together with Rahul Gandhi's SIR plea. The court issued notice but declined tagging for now, with the CJI orally indicating SIR issues will be tackled state-wise, not in a generalized manner. Both carrying outlets are legal-digital; no mainstream-print/broadcast corroboration found.
items.title: SC declines to tag Maharashtra SIR challenge with Rahul Gandhi's plea; will examine state-wise
Abhijeet Dipke detained by Delhi Police ahead of the 5 PM 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Connaught Place
items.summary: Delhi Police detained CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke at ~5:00 PM IST on Friday, minutes ahead of the scheduled 5 PM 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Central Park, Connaught Place (ANI video carried on The Daily Jagran live blog). Police told him "We are placing you under preventive detention," citing Section 163 BNSS prohibitory orders in CP and no NDMC permission for the march (inshorts, published 11:29:15Z). A crowd had already started gathering around Central Park ~4:48 PM despite the closure. This is Dipke's second detention in a week (first: Oct 10, off the Mumbai-Delhi flight). Confirmed internationally by Reuters and CNN; @indianexpress (11:40:20Z) and @timesofindia (11:24:45Z) posted detention footage/graphic on IG. Note (single-source, nationpress FAQ): party legal head Ratna Singh says release-proceedings paperwork for Das/Ranka was completed but delayed by officials, and CJP will challenge the detentions in court.
items.source_name: ANI via The Daily Jagran (live blog); Reuters; CNN; inshorts

items.title: Dipke's video message to PM Modi after police notice: 'Why are you against Tiranga?'
items.summary: Follow-up to the earlier-alerted march-buildup item: the contents of Dipke's ~4:27 PM video message are now public — "Heavy police force deployed at the gate just to stop Tiranga. Why are you against Tiranga, @narendramodi?" (Dipke's own X post via The Daily Jagran live blog). The message was recorded after Delhi Police served him the Section 163 notice at NCP-SCP spokesperson Anish Gawande's residence, asking him not to hold the march; inshorts/latestly carry video of him signing the notice. Gawande backed the march, saying participants planned to unfurl the flag and return peacefully (India Today).
items.source_name: Abhijeet Dipke (X post) via The Daily Jagran (live blog); latestly; inshorts

items.title: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh accuses Congress/INDIA bloc of seeking Bangladesh-style 'regime change' via youth protests
items.summary: At a Lucknow press conference, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh accused Congress and its allies of using the EC/SIR protests to seek a Bangladesh-style 'regime change' and turning youth into 'pawns in the politics of chaos/anarchy' — a 'conspiracy to seize power by inciting anarchy in the country' (PTI via news89). He directly attacked Rahul Gandhi, dismissing his duplicate/fake-voter claims as baseless and noting Congress has filed no formal appeals or evidence; he told Gandhi to respect the mandate and self-introspect (Mirror Now). UP BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary echoed the 'conspiracy to destabilise' line in Lucknow (ANI via devdiscourse). TBS reports Singh's remarks were a response to Prashant Bhushan's statement at a Press Club of India presser yesterday (alongside Dipke and Neha Bora) that they seek regime change 'and there is nothing wrong with it' (single-source). Also in the live blog: WB BJP's Dilip Ghosh accused CJP of disrupting Durga Puja celebrations.
items.source_name: PTI via news89; Mirror Now; TBS; ANI via devdiscourse

items.title: CATCH-UP: DMK MP Kanimozhi joins student organisations' protest in Chennai demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal, SIR withdrawal
items.summary: CATCH-UP (never alerted): DMK MP Kanimozhi joined a student organisations' protest in Chennai demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal and withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls (PTI video via The Daily Jagran live blog, ~12:34 PM IST). Earlier the same day, student organisations and civil society members held an anti-CEC/SIR protest in Chennai (PTI). Kanimozhi accused the Centre of lacking faith in the Constitution, alleged ~1 lakh voters removed in Kolathur against ~20,000 warranted, claimed Maharashtra roll changes benefited BJP, and said the DMK stands with protesting youth (Asianet Newsable/khelja.in, ANI-syndicated). The protest used Periyar-like models as symbolic elements, with VCK's Thol. Thirumavalavan also present (news89 citing India Today).
items.source_name: PTI via The Daily Jagran (live blog); Asianet Newsable (khelja.in); news89 (citing India Today)

items.title: CATCH-UP: CP traders write to PM Modi (and CJI, LoP) over protest losses; claim Rs 250 crore/day hit, 70% footfall drop
items.summary: CATCH-UP (never alerted): trade bodies wrote to PM Modi, the CJI and LoP Rahul Gandhi over protest-related business losses, seeking immediate intervention (ANI via The Daily Jagran live blog, ~4:16 PM IST; Jagran article published 10:25 AM IST). CP traders claim Rs 250 crore/day business loss and up to 70% footfall drop (2-3 lakh daily visitors down to 40,000-50,000) since the Oct-2 protests; New Delhi Traders Association president Atul Bhargava told ANI business fell to 10% during the CJP protest (devdiscourse), and DL Madan (Janpath) said some shops had no first sale for five Navratri days. A restaurant owner separately approached the Delhi HC seeking compensation for protest losses (devdiscourse). The Supreme Court (CJI Surya Kant + Justice Joymalya Bagchi) listed the Kirana Committee/Iron Traders Association writ against the CJP and Congress protests for Oct 26, warning it could intervene — 'We will act' — if restrictions unlawfully hurt business (livemint).
items.source_name: ANI via The Daily Jagran; livemint; devdiscourse

items.title: AISA chief Neha Bora detained en route to Tiranga March
items.summary: All India Students' Association national president Neha Bora was detained by Delhi Police on her way to the 5 PM 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Connaught Place, PTI reported via Daily Jagran's live blog. She is the first of the expanded figures to be detained on march day.

items.title: Dipke served two police notices ahead of detention
items.summary: Delhi Police served CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke two notices on Friday, ANI reported via Daily Jagran's live blog: one under the Delhi Police Act barring him from visiting Central Park under Section 163 of the BNS, and a second from South West Delhi police tied to the Oct-10 airport preventive-custody incident, citing a court directive to avoid public disturbance for one year. Dipke was then placed under preventive detention ahead of the 5 PM march.

The Election Commission will share machine-readable ('readable PDF') draft and final electoral rolls — soft copies, plus addition/deletion/modification supplements — with recognised political parties for the first time, a reversal after years of refusing the demand citing privacy/fudging concerns and a 2018 Supreme Court order that backed its stance. Congress (@INCIndia, Oct 16 X post) claimed the concession as a victory for Rahul Gandhi's long-running demand, saying the ECI had finally 'bowed'. Commentator Mohit Chauhan asked whether the ECI will also release the pre-SIR machine-readable rolls, noting SIR risks burying evidence of earlier deletions.
items.title: ECI to share 'readable' (machine-readable) voter rolls with parties for the first time; Congress claims victory

items.summary: A division bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma declined a CP vendor's urgent plea to restrain Dipke/CJP from holding the Oct 16 'Lehra Do Tiranga' gathering at Central Park, Connaught Place. ASG Chetan Sharma told the court police will take 'appropriate steps' against Dipke given a 'pattern of lawlessness'; the court took the assurance on record and listed the matter for Nov 3.
items.title: Delhi HC refuses to restrain CJP's Oct 16 Connaught Place protest; police assure 'appropriate steps'

items.summary: Delhi Police PRO Neha Yadav said at a press conference that while the march had no permission, police could facilitate a group of 11 people to carry the national flag and sing the national anthem at a suitable location; the public was urged not to join the mass gathering. Prohibitory orders under Sec 163 BNSS remain in force in CP; NDMC shut Central Park for Oct 16-17.
items.title: Delhi Police offers 11-person symbolic flag event, urges public to stay away from CP march

items.source_name: Maktoob Media + Indian Economic Observer + ANI via LatestLY
items.summary: NSUI's overnight protest outside Parliament Street police station — demanding an FIR over alleged police assault on women workers Athira and Ritu two days earlier — ended with detentions: NSUI national president Vinod Jakhar and the IYC president were detained (Jakhar held at Dwarka Sector-23 PS from ~12:00 PM IST Friday, alongside workers held at other stations; some MPs, Youth Congress, Seva Dal colleagues also detained). Jakhar alleged his clothes were torn and he was nearly strangled during the detention.
items.title: NSUI president Vinod Jakhar and IYC president detained during overnight Parliament Street protest

items.summary: The 5 PM march went ahead at Connaught Place despite Dipke's detention: NDTV live reported a large number of protesters gathering at CP amid heavy police deployment. Trendkia's bylined live blog: Neha Bora + co-protesters detained at Mandi House circle (5:37 PM); an SFI-led contingent blocked at Janpath-Tolstoy Marg (5:47 PM); CPI(M) MPs John Brittas, Dr. V Sivadasan and A.A. Rahim with SFI/DYFI/AISF/AIYF marching toward Central Park with tricolours (6:05 PM). A senior police officer (PTI): 'Some protesters have reached Connaught Place and will be removed soon.' Also: protesters gathered at Mumbai's Azad Maidan (police permitted; from 3:55 PM) and student organisations + civil society held an anti-CEC protest in Chennai (PTI).
items.title: Lehra Do Tiranga march went ahead at Connaught Place despite detentions

items.summary: PTI (via 7globe): police sources say Dipke was taken to Jafarpur Kalan police station after his preventive detention. A post on Neha Bora's X account claims she was 'detained alone, taken to unknown location' with no phone on her, adding 'Delhi Police must answer: where is Neha?' and calling it 'once again, an abduction'. A senior police officer confirmed both detentions, calling the situation 'very peaceful'.
items.title: Dipke taken to Jafarpur Kalan PS; Bora's whereabouts unknown, say her aides

items.summary: After Delhi Police detained Abhijeet Dipke and Neha Bora en route to the Tiranga March, former Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal posted on X: 'If we won't hoist the tricolour in our own country, then will we hoist it in Pakistan? Those who have a problem with the Indian tricolour should go to Pakistan.' No second outlet has carried the statement yet.
items.title: Kejriwal reacts to march detentions: 'If we won't hoist the tricolour in our own country, then will we hoist it in Pakistan?'

items.summary: In an X post, senior Congress leader P. Chidambaram claimed SIR was abandoned for the 17 remaining states/UTs (replaced by the customary SSR, with no citizenship documents required) only after the protests and the Supreme Court notice. He asked why 20 states faced SIR with 13.3 crore names removed 'without Due Process', noted the ECI is now running another exercise to include 'left out' voters, and demanded CEC Gyanesh Kumar 'be surcharged for the double expenditure'. The ECI had on Oct 15 ordered SSR in 17 states/UTs (draft roll Nov 12, claims window to Dec 11, final roll Jan 4, 2027).
items.title: Chidambaram: SIR abandoned for 17 states/UTs; 'Gyanesh Kumar should be surcharged for the double expenditure'

items.event_time_ist: Oct 16, 2026 (meeting held Friday; exact time unreported)
items.summary: At a Bengaluru meeting (Legislators' Home) led by KPCC president B.K. Hariprasad, INDIA Bloc's Karnataka constituents launched a 'Save the Vote, Save the Nation' anti-SIR campaign, demanded CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation and set a protest calendar: a large protest at Ramlila Maidan, New Delhi on Nov 1; a major rally in Bengaluru on Nov 5; then district/taluk-level expansion. A coordination committee (Congress, CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, SP, Forward Bloc) will run it.
items.title: INDIA Bloc Karnataka launches anti-SIR campaign: Nov 1 Ramlila Maidan protest, Nov 5 Bengaluru rally

items.summary: CATCH-UP (never alerted): at the national INDIA bloc meeting on Wednesday, Congress pitched a 'massive agitation to save democracy'; sources said a draft notice for a motion to remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha was ready and would be deliberated for approval; K.C. Venugopal said an action plan would be formalized after suggestions. DMK and AAP skipped the meeting; Akhilesh Yadav was absent over Rajya Sabha nominations. (Distinct from the Oct-13 symbolic 'impeach the CEC' mock-parliament proposal.)
items.title: CATCH-UP: INDIA Bloc discussed draft removal-motion notice against CEC at Wednesday meeting
SC issues notices to Rahul, Kharge, Akhilesh and others over Oct-12 march; CJI: 'Nobody can browbeat us'
items.summary: CATCH-UP (never alerted): at Thursday's hearing, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notices on pleas seeking a regulatory framework for protests and processions near judicial complexes and criminal contempt proceedings against Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav, Mahua Moitra and others over their Oct-12 'March for Democracy' to the apex court; CJI observed 'nobody can browbeat us' and that judges are not sitting in ivory towers; ordered preservation of CCTV footage of SC premises; separately issued notice to the ECI, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the two ECs on the opposition leaders' SIR plea itself; declined to act on a contempt plea against Kerala Congress over remarks on the CJI.

items.title: SC orders Sanjay Raut to explain remarks against CJI; AG clears criminal contempt move
items.summary: CATCH-UP (never alerted): the same bench said the INDIA bloc's SIR plea would be entertained at Sanjay Raut's instance only provisionally, subject to him explaining his conduct over claims that the CJI and 60-70 judges played badminton with BJP leaders in London; Raut is petitioner no.6 in the joint plea. Separately, AG R Venkataramani granted consent to the Supreme Court Bar Association to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against Raut and journalist Nikhil Wagle over their remarks on the CJI and judiciary; SCBA has filed a criminal contempt petition; Wagle deleted his post and tendered an unconditional apology to the CJI and the court. Two more opposition leaders — VCK's Thol. Thirumavalavan and NC's Sajjat Ahmad Kichloo — joined the petition, taking the petitioners to 13.

items.summary: A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi on Friday issued show-cause notices to Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut and journalist Nikhil Wagle in criminal contempt proceedings over remarks targeting the CJI and the judiciary, on a plea filed by the Supreme Court Bar Association after AG R Venkataramani granted consent. The bench exempted both from personal appearance for now and will consider their explanations before deciding next steps. Raut — petitioner no. 6 in the INDIA-bloc SIR writ — had alleged the CJI and 60-70 judges played badminton with BJP leaders in London; the AG noted the circulated photos were actually from Thyagaraj Stadium, Delhi (Nov 2025). Wagle had deleted his abusive X post and apologized.
items.title: SC issues show-cause notices to Sanjay Raut, Nikhil Wagle in criminal contempt over remarks against CJI

items.summary: Congress workers in Kerala's Palakkad on Friday staged a mock funeral of CEC Gyanesh Kumar — carrying a mock bier from the DCC office to the Stadium Bus Stand, burning his garlanded photograph on a pyre with Hindu-cremation-style rituals, then dumping the 'ashes' into a toilet — to protest the ECI's SIR handling. The act drew attention as Congress had earlier criticized the SFI for a similar mock funeral of a Palakkad college principal. Part of the nationwide Congress campaign demanding Kumar's removal over SIR.
items.title: Congress workers in Palakkad stage mock funeral of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, dump 'ashes' in toilet

Sanjay Raut publicly apologizes after SC issues criminal-contempt show-cause notice
items.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut — petitioner no. 6 in the INDIA-bloc SIR writ — publicly apologized Friday evening after the SC bench (CJI Surya Kant + Justice Joymalya Bagchi) issued show-cause notices to him and journalist Nikhil Wagle in criminal-contempt proceedings on SCBA's plea (AG R Venkataramani's consent). Speaking to reporters, Raut said neither he nor his party intended to disrespect the judiciary: 'If the Supreme Court feels I have made any inappropriate remarks against it, there is nothing wrong in apologizing to the institution that protects the Indian Constitution,' adding he is ready to formally apologize. He also used the moment to reiterate his demand that the judiciary address the alleged deletion of 13 crore voters and to complain that the Sena name/symbol dispute has dragged on 4.5 years across four CJIs. Follows the alerted 16:06Z show-cause arc (sc-raut-wagle-showcause-oct16). Published 2026-10-16T17:55:12Z; missed by the 18:24Z/19:14Z/19:46Z runs. Covering outlets: India Bytes (this statement); LiveLaw independently reported Raut expressed regret in an earlier ANI interview (pre-notice). Confidence single-sourced.

The All India Students' Association (AISA) called its Mandi House demonstration (5:15 PM, Oct 16, led by president Neha Bora) around three explicit demands: the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, the revocation of the SIR electoral-roll revision, and the scrapping of the 2023 Election Commissioner Appointment Act. AISA activists and students later marched from Mandi House toward Connaught Place with the tricolour; Bora and others were detained at the Mandi House roundabout.
items.title: AISA's Mandi House demo pressed three demands: CEC resignation, SIR rollback, scrapping the 2023 EC Appointment Act

items.summary: AISA functionaries confirmed advocates were able to meet detained AISA president Neha Bora at the RK Puram police station. This is the first reported legal-team contact with Bora since her detention at Mandi House (~5:40 PM IST, Oct 16). No second outlet has carried this yet.
items.title: Advocates meet detained Neha Bora at RK Puram; AISA says medication being denied, no word on release

(2) BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi called the Connaught Place rally a 'conspiracy to destabilise' India's economy during the festive season and urged students not to become 'pawns' (LatestLY, first appeared 10:28 PM IST Oct 16). items.title: BJP counter-offensive Friday: Brij Bhushan alleges Musk is 'orchestrating' the protests; Trivedi alleges economy-destabilisation plot; Delhi BJP claims 'foreign sponsors'

Later the same day, police granted conditional approval: the march — organised with Jagruta Karnataka, AISA Karnataka and My Vote, My Right in support of Das and Ranka — proceeded from Town Hall to the Quit India Memorial with hundreds braving persistent rain. Conditions imposed: no protest slogans against political parties/organisations/communities/individuals, and protest placards restricted at the destination (Mirror Now).
items.title: Bengaluru: Town Hall Tiranga march denied in the morning, then granted conditional approval — hundreds marched in rain

items.summary: All India Students' Association president Neha Bora was released early Saturday morning after completing formalities under Section 65 of the Delhi Police Act, Delhi Police said (via PTI). She was detained at Mandi House on Friday evening en route to the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march. In her first statement after release she alleged protesters are detained without valid reason and held for hours, questioned overnight detentions of women ('ought to be released after sunset'), said lawyers were denied access to her for hours, and demanded Abhijeet Dipke's immediate release plus Gyanesh Kumar's impeachment and a halt to SIR.

items.title: Abhijeet Dipke under BNSS preventive arrest; to be produced before SEM court today
items.summary: Delhi Police placed CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke under preventive arrest (action under BNSS Sections 126 and 170, breach of peace) after detaining him Friday evening ahead of the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Connaught Place. Police will produce him before the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court — the same court that granted him conditional bail on Oct 10 — later today. CJP legal head Ratna Singh alleged Dipke's location remains unknown to his team and lawyers have not been allowed to meet him; Zee24Taas/Saam TV clips show CJP supporters asking 'Where have you kept Abhijeet Dipke?' outside police stations.

items.title: CATCH-UP (never alerted): Kharge, Ramesh escalate SIR fight — Kharge accuses Shah of branding ~13.3 crore Indians 'infiltrators'; Ramesh dubs SIR 'Shah Instigated Removal'
items.summary: CATCH-UP: these Oct-14 statements fell through the cracks of that day's runs and were never alerted. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge posted on X accusing HM Amit Shah of insulting Indian identity by describing the ~13.3 crore people allegedly excluded by SIR as 'infiltrators'; he condemned the Jantar Mantar protest curbs ('First vote theft, then theft of the right to protest'), accused the BJP of an authoritarian agenda, and accused the government of shielding CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Jairam Ramesh (two X posts) dubbed SIR the 'Shah Instigated Removal' and posed three questions to Shah: how many infiltrators were detected, deleted, and deported after ~100 crore Indians went through SIR — asking whether the government suggests 14 crore Indians are infiltrators. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav issued a poetic 'One voice of One India' X post against alleged electoral fraud. Context: Shah on Tuesday (Oct 13) had said the opposition should be ready for a 'crushing defeat' in 2029 and claimed the country could see through Rahul Gandhi's 'plan' to get infiltrators registered as voters.

items.summary: New corroborated details flesh out Friday's Oct-16 detentions (already alerted): The Indian Express reports more than 20 police personnel visited Abhijeet Dipke's Karol Bagh residence and served a notice barring the Connaught Place demonstration (citing disruption to traders, commuters, patients; CP not a designated protest site). Dipke was detained ~4:50 PM IST Oct 16 after leaving the residence; on being stopped he asked 'I am alone. Why are you stopping me?' and unfurled the national flag before officers moved him into a police vehicle. Police sources said he was taken to Jaffarpur Kalan PS in southwest Delhi, where preventive detention was considered. Separately, AISA claims Neha Bora was moved between locations across Delhi for ~5 hours after her Mandi House detention and taken to RK Puram PS, where lawyers who reached around midnight were not allowed to meet her (via The Hindu). items.summary: A DMK parliamentary party meeting at Anna Arivalayam (Chennai) today, chaired by M.K. Stalin, adopted a resolution demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal: 'He must be removed and subjected to an appropriate inquiry' (for SIR voter deletions overriding fellow ECs' objections). Demanded a return to paper ballots (EVM/VVPAT discrepancies), a representation to the President seeking complete SIR cancellation before the Assembly elections, and future polls on existing rolls. Backed CJP/student-group protests as 'a greater impact than those organised by the Congress' (dig at Congress). DMK MP Kanimozhi said 'We have already supported CJP'; she attended the Oct-16 Chennai Rajarathinam Stadium student-group protest demanding Kumar's resignation.

items.event_time_ist: ~5:00 PM IST, Oct 16 (BBC report published ~4:42 AM IST, Oct 17)
items.summary: BBC on-the-ground reporting from the Oct-16 'Lehra Do Tiranga' crackdown: BBC journalists personally saw officers surround Dipke as he approached his car and force him into a police vehicle, with some supporters trying to stop the vehicle from leaving. Hundreds had gathered in Connaught Place waving Indian flags and shouting slogans despite a heavy security presence; police sealed off Central Park and deployed thousands of police and paramilitary personnel. The BBC notes the police response was 'more restrained than during last weekend's sweeping crackdown.' CJP spokesperson Mehr Pasricha told the BBC: 'They may detain three people, but how will they stop 30 tomorrow? How will they stop 300 leaders?' Anish Gawande, the NCP-SCP spokesperson who had been hosting Dipke, said: 'Detaining a lone man walking with the national flag in his hand is a bit of a joke.' Police have not publicly confirmed the grounds for Dipke's detention or responded to CJP's latest allegations.
items.title: BBC eyewitness: officers forced Dipke into van; Mehr — 'how will they stop 300 leaders?'; Gawande — detention 'a bit of a joke'

items.summary: India Today Digital's ground report on Friday's 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Connaught Place: the protest was rudderless, with no CJP functionary visibly leading more than two hours after Abhijeet Dipke's detention and no apparent 'plan B'. Around 5:25 PM, ~100 protesters carrying the Tricolour marched a circuit of CP's inner circle from Palika Market Gate 1; ~100-120 SFI members gathered near Tolstoy Marg; AISA chief Neha Bora was detained from Mandi House by 5:15 PM. CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas (reached CP ~7:30 PM) was the only prominent leader its reporter saw - though other outlets also report MPs V Sivadasan, AA Rahim and Santhosh Kumar joining. Hundreds were detained by 8 PM. An IPS officer is quoted saying the national flag was 'acting as a shield', which is why police avoided moving against the gathering despite Section 163 BNSS orders. RAF personnel were stationed every 300-400 m with batons, tear gas shells and firearms; dozens of drones hovered over CP. In Mumbai, I-Today reports 'barely a few dozen' turned up at Azad Maidan (capacity 5,000-6,000). The piece also recalls a similar CJP leadership vacuum at the July 20 protest.
items.title: India Today ground report: Friday's Tiranga march at CP was 'rudderless' with no CJP command centre

items.summary: Several women's organisations (AIDWA, NFIW, AIPWA, ALIFA) marched to Delhi Police headquarters Saturday over alleged sexual violence and police brutality against women during the anti-CEC/SIR protests. CPI leader Annie Raja told ANI the Centre is 'using sexual assault as a weapon' to silence women protesters, demanded action against the personnel involved and the resignation of Home Minister Amit Shah; she linked the march to the SIR-rollback and CEC-resignation demands, and noted Ankita Bhandari's parents joined. A parallel demonstration outside the HQ by SFI, AIMSS and KYS activists alleged police 'touching the women protestors' body parts inappropriately' (IANS). Delhi Police's counter: it slammed 'misleading social media claims' and said three women journalists' Oct-3 complaints were transferred to the Crime Branch for enquiry.
items.title: Women's groups march to Delhi Police HQ over alleged sexual violence at anti-CEC protests

items.summary: The planned 2 PM Press Club of India -> Jantar Mantar march is underway: two independent on-the-ground Instagram videos show demonstrators gathered outside the Press Club of India with 'RECLAIM JANTAR MANTAR' and 'GYANESH KUMAR MUST RESIGN' placards; one video (~2:30 PM) shows Delhi Police yellow barricades containing the crowd near the Press Club, speakers addressing protesters and media. A WatchDog TV reporter interviewed a protester demanding Jantar Mantar's reopening as a protest site and continued daily protests. A third small account's narration claims Neha Bora is leading the march - unverified.
items.title: 2 PM Press Club -> Jantar Mantar march materialises; protesters at Press Club of India

items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has been PRODUCED before the Special Executive Magistrate court at Mandir Marg police station, after his Friday preventive arrest under BNSS Sections 126 and 170 ahead of the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Connaught Place. LiveLaw's live-update log records the production at 3:29 PM IST with 'heavy security outside Mandir Marg police station'; The Daily Jagran (original byline, updated 3:15 PM IST) confirms he was brought before the SEM court. The SEM's ruling — whether he is bound down, released, or held — is not yet reported. Ratna Singh, CJP's legal head, had demanded his release, calling the arrest unlawful since he 'merely urged people to unfurl the Tiranga'.
items.title: Dipke PRODUCED before SEM court at Mandir Marg (~3:29 PM IST); ruling still awaited

items.summary: CATCH-UP (event before this run, never logged in the feed): Booker Prize-winning author Salman Rushdie publicly backed the CJP at a fundraising dinner for the Asian American Writers Workshop in New York on Thursday night, calling the youth agitation 'the most hopeful moment for a very long time' and urging the audience to 'celebrate the cockroach' — 'India is boiling,' he said. Delhi SEM court grants conditional bail to CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke
items.summary: The Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court at Mandir Marg granted bail to Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday, after his Oct-16 preventive arrest under BNSS Secs 126/170 ahead of the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at CP Central Park. Delhi Police confirmed he will be released after signing a peace bond (ANI); full bail conditions awaited. Dipke's legal team confirmed the order. This resolves the ~8-hour SEM wait; his lawyer Ratna Singh had demanded release, calling the arrest unlawful and alleging his whereabouts were undisclosed and lawyers denied access.

items.summary: INDIA bloc MPs on Saturday condemned the Oct-16/17 detentions of ECI/SIR protesters in Delhi as an attack on democracy. CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP V. Sivadasan alleged detentions were carried out 'only because of directions from the Home Ministry,' that detainees (hundreds of students, including women) were not informed of reasons for hours and were manhandled; 'Our fight will continue.' SP RS MP Awadhesh Prasad drew an undeclared-Emergency parallel; Congress spokesperson Surendra Rajput called the arrests of Tiranga-march participants 'colonial-era policing' by 'followers of the British'; Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Priyanka Chaturvedi invoked Sushma Swaraj and Arun Jaitley on the right to dissent and flagged the Jantar Mantar de-notification as weakening democratic foundations.
items.title: INDIA bloc leaders condemn Oct-16/17 ECI protest detentions; allege Home Ministry orders, manhandling
CATCH-UP: Delhi Police registered 25 FIRs over SIR protests since Oct 2 — Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra among those named (The Hindu)
items.summary: Delhi Police have registered 25 FIRs in connection with the series of protests in the national capital since October 2, 2026, per police sources, covering alleged vandalism of public property, assaults and scuffles involving police personnel, obstruction of government work, and violations of prohibitory orders under BNSS Section 163 in the New Delhi district. Several political leaders, including Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, have been named in the cases. The tally includes the Oct-7 FIR against Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other INDIA bloc MPs for allegedly entering Akashvani Bhavan premises without permission during their march toward Nirvachan Sadan (ECI HQ). DCP Shrishti Pandey said protests were not permitted at Jantar Mantar or any other location while the restrictions remained in force. The figure dates to an Oct-9 ANI wire report ('till Thursday') and was republished/updated by The Hindu on Oct 17 — it was never evaluated in earlier runs, hence this catch-up.

items.title: Indian Express reports Tihar jail-logistics details for Das and Ranka
items.summary: The Indian Express reports that Saurav Das is inmate No. 3752 in ward 3 of Tihar Jail No. 2 (the same jail block where Umar Khalid is currently housed, in a different cell, and where Arvind Kejriwal was previously held) and Ashutosh Ranka is inmate No. 1784 in ward 15 of Jail No. 4, after being moved from Jail No. 2. Both are in high-security wards with 'NO OTHER INMATE ALLOWED', under CCTV surveillance; police cited 'serious apprehension' they would reoffend if bailed. The report says the two were visited in jail by CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and legal head Ratna Singh, implying Dipke is out after his conditional bail. News18 Marathi independently reports the two leaders are in separate wards under strict security; Inshorts carries the Indian Express details.

items.title: Delhi Police claims woman protester slapped a CRPF constable during Oct-16 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march; CCTV review underway, legal action planned
items.summary: Delhi Police has released video of an alleged assault near Rajiv Chowk Metro Station Gate No. 6 (by Palika Bazaar) during CJP's 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march on the evening of Oct 16. Police claim a woman posing as a YouTuber slapped a woman CRPF constable amid the gathering, and say CCTV and other footage are being examined to identify those involved and initiate legal action. The claim is carried by Republic Bharat (IG segment posted ~9:26 PM IST Oct 17), NDTV and India TV, all with police-source framing. Caution: the allegation is police-sourced and the video is not independently authenticated; no mainstream-print, independent-digital, wire or fact-checker coverage of this specific claim was found, and it is one allegation amid conflicting viral-video narratives from Oct-16 detentions (both sides allege assaults).
